sets.title: Bookbinding workshop poster
sets.passage: The Art Club is holding a bookbinding workshop on Thursday, 14 March, in Room 12. It starts at 3:30 and finishes at 5:00. You will learn to fold paper, sew the pages together and add a strong cover to make your own notebook. We will give you everything you need, so you just have to bring yourself. The workshop is free, but there are only twenty places. To sign up, write your name on the list outside the art room by Tuesday. Please ask Ms Hesketh if you have any questions.

items.prompt: In the poster, the word "places" is closest in meaning to
choices: towns or cities
spaces for people
positions in a race
homes to live in
items.why: there are only twenty places. To sign up, write your name on the list
items.explanation: "spaces for people" is correct: the poster says "there are only twenty places. To sign up, write your name on the list", so a place is a space for one student in the workshop.

distractor_rationales.choice: towns or cities
distractor_rationales.reason: "towns or cities" is a real meaning of the word, but the workshop happens in one room, "in Room 12", and the places are something students take by signing up: "To sign up, write your name on the list".

distractor_rationales.choice: positions in a race
distractor_rationales.reason: "positions in a race" is a real meaning of the word, but the poster describes a workshop where "You will learn to fold paper", not a race; the places are filled when students "write your name on the list".

distractor_rationales.choice: homes to live in
distractor_rationales.reason: "homes to live in" is a real meaning of the word, but nobody lives at the workshop; the places are limited spots students claim when they "write your name on the list outside the art room".

sets.title: Note about helping at the fruit stall
sets.passage:
Kirra,
Your grandpa phoned this morning. His back hurts again, so he asked if you could help at his fruit stall at the market today. He needs you there by nine, not ten like last time, because the market opens an hour earlier in summer. He will stay until it closes at two. Bring a jacket, as the stall is in the shade all morning. He will pay you and give you a bag of plums to take home. I am taking your brother to swimming practice and will be back at noon.
Mum

items.prompt: Why does Kirra need to arrive at the stall earlier than last time?
choices: Her grandfather's stall is moving to a sunnier part of the market.
She has to be at swimming practice later today.
The market starts earlier at this time of year.
Her grandfather wants to leave the market before lunch.
items.correct_answer: The market starts earlier at this time of year.
items.why: because the market opens an hour earlier in summer
items.explanation: "The market starts earlier at this time of year." is correct: the note says he needs her "by nine, not ten like last time, because the market opens an hour earlier in summer".

distractor_rationales.choice: Her grandfather wants to leave the market before lunch.
distractor_rationales.reason: "Her grandfather wants to leave the market before lunch." is wrong because the note says "He will stay until it closes at two".

distractor_rationales.choice: Her grandfather's stall is moving to a sunnier part of the market.
distractor_rationales.reason: "Her grandfather's stall is moving to a sunnier part of the market." is wrong because the note says "the stall is in the shade all morning"; the reason for the time is "because the market opens an hour earlier in summer".

distractor_rationales.choice: She has to be at swimming practice later today.
distractor_rationales.reason: "She has to be at swimming practice later today." is wrong because swimming practice is for her brother: "I am taking your brother to swimming practice".

sets.title: The picture signs of Hallowmere
sets.passage:
Three hundred years ago, the main street of Hallowmere looked very different from today. Above almost every shop door hung a painted wooden sign with a picture on it. A baker showed a loaf of bread, a shoemaker showed a boot, and a locksmith showed a large golden key. These pictures rarely changed, and a shop often kept the same sign for a hundred years, even after a new family took it over.

The pictures had a practical purpose. Many people in the town could not read, so a written name over the door would have helped only a few customers. A picture could be understood by everyone, including farmers who came in from nearby villages on market day.

The signs also worked as addresses. Houses had no numbers yet, so people gave directions by naming the pictures. A letter might be sent to the tailor beside the green hen, and the messenger would know exactly where to go.

Over time, however, the signs became a problem. Shopkeepers competed to hang the biggest ones, and some stretched halfway across the street. They blocked light from upper windows and creaked loudly in the wind. In 1771, after a heavy sign fell and injured a horse, the town council ordered that every sign be fixed flat against the wall. Later, when the town began to number its houses, many shops replaced their pictures with painted names.

items.prompt: According to the passage, why did the signs on the main street grow so large?
choices: Painters charged the same amount for a sign of any size.
Visitors from the villages found small signs hard to see.
Shop owners were trying to do better than one another.
The town council asked shops to make their signs bigger.
items.correct_answer: Shop owners were trying to do better than one another.
items.why: Shopkeepers competed to hang the biggest ones
items.explanation: "Shop owners were trying to do better than one another." is correct: the passage says "Shopkeepers competed to hang the biggest ones", so each owner was trying to beat the others.

distractor_rationales.choice: Visitors from the villages found small signs hard to see.
distractor_rationales.reason: "Visitors from the villages found small signs hard to see." is wrong because the passage gives a different reason for the size: "Shopkeepers competed to hang the biggest ones"; the villagers are mentioned only as people who could understand pictures.

distractor_rationales.choice: The town council asked shops to make their signs bigger.
distractor_rationales.reason: "The town council asked shops to make their signs bigger." is wrong because the council acted against the signs: it "ordered that every sign be fixed flat against the wall"; the size came from the fact that "Shopkeepers competed to hang the biggest ones".

distractor_rationales.choice: Painters charged the same amount for a sign of any size.
distractor_rationales.reason: "Painters charged the same amount for a sign of any size." is wrong because the passage explains the size in another way: "Shopkeepers competed to hang the biggest ones".

items.prompt: In paragraph 4, the word "fixed" is closest in meaning to
choices: repaired
decided
attached
prepared
items.why: every sign be fixed flat against the wall
items.explanation: "attached" is correct: after "a heavy sign fell and injured a horse", the council ordered "every sign be fixed flat against the wall", meaning attached firmly to the wall so it could not hang out and fall.

distractor_rationales.choice: repaired
distractor_rationales.reason: "repaired" is a real meaning of the word, but the order was about where signs went after one "fell and injured a horse": every sign had to sit "flat against the wall", which is about attaching, not mending.

distractor_rationales.choice: decided
distractor_rationales.reason: "decided" is a real meaning of the word (a price can be fixed), but a sign cannot be decided "flat against the wall"; the phrase describes where the sign is held.

distractor_rationales.choice: prepared
distractor_rationales.reason: "prepared" is a real meaning of the word (to fix a meal), but a sign prepared "flat against the wall" makes no sense after a sign "fell and injured a horse"; the order was to hold signs to walls.

distractor_rationales.reason: "Farmers who visited from nearby villages could understand them." is stated: "A picture could be understood by everyone, including farmers who came in from nearby villages".

distractor_rationales.reason: "They made a creaking noise when it was windy." is stated: the signs "creaked loudly in the wind".

sets.title: Pricing the woodwork club's spoons
sets.passage:
Every December, our school turns the sports hall into a winter fair, and each club gets one table. Last year was the first time the woodwork club took part. There were six of us, and since September we had been carving small wooden spoons in the workshop after school. Each spoon took about three hours: sawing a rough shape from a block, hollowing the bowl with a curved knife, then sanding until the handle felt smooth. By the day of the fair we had forty of them.

We argued for a week about the price. Hugo said nobody would pay more than two dollars for a spoon, while Imogen wanted five. Our teacher, Mr Lomax, refused to help and told us to decide for ourselves. In the end we chose two dollars, wrote the price on a card and waited. The spoons were gone in less than an hour, and at first we were thrilled. Then Imogen counted the money: eighty dollars, which was barely more than we had spent on wood and sandpaper. Worse, several buyers had called the spoons cute and asked if a machine had made them.

That evening I worked it out. We had sold around a hundred and twenty hours of careful work for little more than the cost of the wood, and the low price had made people think the spoons were cheap objects rather than things made slowly by hand. Our price had told a story about the spoons, and it was the wrong story.

This year we took forty spoons to the fair again, but we did two things differently. First, we brought a log, a knife and a half-finished spoon, and took turns carving at the table while people watched. Second, we raised the price to twelve dollars and kept it there all day, with a card explaining that each spoon takes about three hours to make. I was sure we would go home with a full box.

We did not. We sold twenty-five spoons, fewer than last year, but they brought in three hundred dollars, and we used the money to buy a second set of carving knives. More surprising was the way people behaved. Instead of grabbing a spoon and walking away, they stood at the table and asked questions. An old man told us that his father had carved spoons from apple wood, and he showed us how his father used to hold the knife. Several buyers turned the spoons over in their hands for a long time before choosing one, as if the choice mattered.

Near the end of the afternoon, a girl from year seven asked if she could join the club. Mr Lomax says the real lesson of the day was about business, but I am not so sure. I think the price of a handmade thing is also a message about it. Last year our message was that the spoons were cheap toys. This year it was that someone had spent an afternoon on each one, and people listened.

items.prompt: What is the passage mainly about?
choices: How the club sold more spoons this year by lowering the price and carving faster
How the club spent the money from this year's fair on a second set of carving knives
How school clubs can earn useful money by selling the crafts they make at school fairs
How showing the work and charging more changed how buyers treated the club's spoons
items.correct_answer: How showing the work and charging more changed how buyers treated the club's spoons
items.why: I think the price of a handmade thing is also a message about it
items.explanation: "How showing the work and charging more changed how buyers treated the club's spoons" is correct: the first year's low price made buyers ask "if a machine had made them"; this year the club carved "at the table while people watched" and charged more, and people "stood at the table and asked questions". The writer concludes "the price of a handmade thing is also a message about it".

distractor_rationales.choice: How school clubs can earn useful money by selling the crafts they make at school fairs
distractor_rationales.reason: "How school clubs can earn useful money by selling the crafts they make at school fairs" is too general: the passage is about one club and what its price told buyers, ending "the price of a handmade thing is also a message about it".

distractor_rationales.choice: How the club spent the money from this year's fair on a second set of carving knives
distractor_rationales.reason: "How the club spent the money from this year's fair on a second set of carving knives" is one detail from paragraph 5: "we used the money to buy a second set of carving knives".

distractor_rationales.choice: How the club sold more spoons this year by lowering the price and carving faster
distractor_rationales.reason: "How the club sold more spoons this year by lowering the price and carving faster" is wrong on both points: they sold "twenty-five spoons, fewer than last year" after they "raised the price to twelve dollars".

items.prompt: What can be inferred about the spoons the club took to this year's fair?
choices: They took less time to make than last year's spoons.
A number of them were still unsold when the fair ended.

items.correct_answer: A number of them were still unsold when the fair ended.
items.why: This year we took forty spoons to the fair again
items.explanation: "A number of them were still unsold when the fair ended." is correct: the club "took forty spoons to the fair again" but "sold twenty-five spoons", so about fifteen were left.

distractor_rationales.choice: They took less time to make than last year's spoons.
distractor_rationales.reason: "They took less time to make than last year's spoons." is contradicted: the card said "each spoon takes about three hours to make", the same as last year, when "Each spoon took about three hours".

distractor_rationales.choice: There were fewer of them than the club had the year before.
distractor_rationales.reason: "There were fewer of them than the club had the year before." is contradicted: "we took forty spoons to the fair again", and last year "we had forty of them".

distractor_rationales.choice: They were priced lower than the first year's spoons.
distractor_rationales.reason: "They were priced lower than the first year's spoons." is contradicted: last year "we chose two dollars", and this year "we raised the price to twelve dollars".
